title: Reading common antenatal blood results
summary: A quick explainer for common antenatal blood tests — not a substitute for full interpretation by the responsible clinician.

blocks.heading: Full blood count (FBC)
bullets: VERIFY local haemoglobin thresholds for offering iron supplementation, as these differ by trimester.

blocks.heading: Blood group and antibody screen
bullets: Identifies Rhesus status and any red cell antibodies that may need additional fetal monitoring.
Rhesus-negative women are usually offered anti-D prophylaxis — VERIFY local dosing schedule.

blocks.heading: Infectious disease screening
bullets: HIV, hepatitis B, and syphilis screening are offered to all women.
Results need timely follow-up, and partner notification/support where a result is positive — per local pathway.

blocks.heading: Haemoglobinopathy screening
bullets: Sickle cell and thalassaemia screening is offered based on a family origin questionnaire and/or risk — VERIFY local pathway.

blocks.heading: OGTT (glucose tolerance test)
bullets: VERIFY current diagnostic glucose thresholds locally, as these are periodically reviewed.

blocks.heading: This is general orientation only
bullets: Always discuss an abnormal result with the responsible obstetric/midwifery team rather than acting on a single value in isolation.
